Colossal Biosciences – a futuristic startup working to bring back extinct species including the woolly mammoth – is suing one of its former top scientists for allegedly stealing trade secrets and sharing the data with competing labs.

In a lawsuit filed Friday morning in Texas federal court in Austin, Colossal accused James Kehler, formerly its vice president of animal sciences and later of BioSynergy, of “dishonesty, greed, and the betrayal of the confidential science at the heart of Colossal’s mission.”

The Dallas-based firm – which has so far succeeded in creating “woolly mice” that bear woolly mammoth traits and gray wolves similar to the extinct dire wolf – claimed Kehler breached three of the contracts he signed with the company after he left for rival labs.

Forensic analysis of Kehler’s Colossal work laptop found that prior to leaving the company, he moved files containing confidential information to a personal cloud account and multiple personal devices, the suit alleged.

Kehler did not immediately respond to The Post’s request for comment.

As a vice president at Colossal, Kehler – who lives in Maryland – had access to the company’s most sensitive scientific information, including data on its avian programs, like work on the dodo bird and the moa, a large, wingless bird formerly found in New Zealand, according to the lawsuit.

Around April 14, 2026, after resigning from Colossal, Kehler joined Neion Bio – a competing lab – as Head of Avian Sciences and “used and disclosed Colossal trade secret and confidential information,” the suit alleged.

He has also been linked to Felix Pets, a startup that claims to use gene-editing technology to develop hypoallergenic cats – a process that “depends on the same research and know-how underlying Colossal’s de-extinction work,” according to the suit.

Colossal is seeking damages, alleging Kehler “pivoted from scientist to thief.” The lab argued that the safeguarding of its proprietary info is key to its efforts to bring back extinct species whose ecosystems have been harmed without them.

It is currently working on the woolly mammoth; dodo; thylacine, a cat-like carnivore with massive jaws also known as the Tasmanian tiger; and dire wolf, a 150-pound-plus creature with thicker legs, wider heads and broader shoulders than today’s wolves.

The startup raised $200 million in a January 2025 funding round led by TWG Global – the investment firm co-founded by Mark Walter and Thomas Tull – that hiked its valuation to $10.2 billion.

Notable investors include Peter Jackson and Fran Walsh, the Oscar-winning film duo behind “The Lord of the Rings” and “The Hobbit,” and hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones.

Colossal has raised at least $435 million since it was founded in 2021 by billionaire entrepreneur Ben Lamm and geneticist George Church, a professor at Harvard and MIT.

“Colossal’s trade secrets and confidential information are the core of its competitive advantage and its ability to achieve its de-extinction mission,” the company said in its complaint.

“The unauthorized use or disclosure of that information – particularly to a competitor – would allow others to replicate in days or weeks what took Colossal years to develop, and at a fraction of the cost. Such unauthorized use or disclosure would inflict severe and irreparable harm on Colossal and on the goals it exists to achieve.”

At its Dallas lab, Colossal said its scientists process tissue samples from endangered animals, edit genomes and work to reprogram stem cells with the goal of undoing a large-scale loss of biodiversity, revive extinct species and preserve endangered species.

Colossal Biosciences - یک استارت آپ آینده نگر که برای بازگرداندن گونه های منقرض شده از جمله ماموت پشمالو کار می کند - از یکی از دانشمندان برتر سابق خود به اتهام سرقت اسرار تجاری و به اشتراک گذاری داده ها با آزمایشگاه های رقیب شکایت کرده است. در شکایتی که صبح روز جمعه در دادگاه فدرال تگزاس در آستین تنظیم شد، کولوسال، جیمز کهلر، معاون سابق رئیس علوم حیوانات و بعداً BioSynergy را به "بی صداقتی، طمع، و خیانت به علم محرمانه در قلب ماموریت کولوسال" متهم کرد. این شرکت مستقر در دالاس - که تا کنون موفق به ایجاد "موش های پشمالو" شده است که دارای ویژگی های ماموت پشمالو و گرگ های خاکستری مشابه گرگ منقرض شده هستند - ادعا کرد که کهلر پس از رفتن به آزمایشگاه های رقیب، سه قرارداد را که با شرکت امضا کرده بود نقض کرد. بررسی قانونی لپ‌تاپ کار عظیم Kehler نشان داد که او قبل از ترک شرکت، فایل‌های حاوی اطلاعات محرمانه را به یک حساب ابری شخصی و چندین دستگاه شخصی منتقل کرده است. طبق این دادخواست، کهلر - که در مریلند زندگی می کند - به عنوان معاون رئیس جمهور در Colossal، به حساس ترین اطلاعات علمی این شرکت، از جمله داده های مربوط به برنامه های پرندگان آن، مانند کار بر روی پرنده dodo و moa، پرنده بزرگ و بدون بال که قبلا در نیوزیلند یافت شده بود، دسترسی داشت. در حدود 14 آوریل 2026، پس از بررسی مجدد Kehler.

Troy Aikman is one of many UCLA Bruins alumni who is stoked about the football team’s undefeated 8-0 record this season.

Aikman is less stoked about his alma mater’s mediocre attendance at home games this season, which was made apparent during No. 8-ranked UCLA’s 27-0 win over Nevada last weekend.

UCLA’s iconic Rose Bowl Stadium can fit 90,888, but only 24,611 were present for the Bruins’ eighth win against Nevada. Aikman admitted this irked him during an appearance on Dallas’ 96.7 “The Ticket” show on Thursday.

“Little embarrassing that we were 7-0 going into last week’s game and, they shoot it pretty low [on TV] so you can’t really tell when you’re watching the game — I’m told there was about 20-25,000 people at the game,” Aikman said, per Awful Announcing.

“So when you have a stadium at the Rose Bowl that holds over 100,000, 25,000, it may as well be empty as opposed to some other stadiums that maybe hold 40,000,” he added.

“We’ve got to get people going to games, we’ve got to get them excited about it. And then you say, ‘Well, how do you get them excited? If 7-0 doesn’t get them excited, what will?’ I don’t know the answer to that.”

24,611 is a respectable amount of fans, which Aikman alluded to.

But the Rose Bowl Stadium makes 24,611 look minuscule, especially for one of the country’s best college football teams.

Nevertheless, the Bruins will continue pushing forward. They play at Minnesota in a tricky Big Ten matchup on Saturday morning before returning home to face Illinois.
news.content:
پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. تروی آیکمن یکی از بسیاری از فارغ التحصیلان UCLA Bruins است که از رکورد شکست ناپذیر 8-0 تیم فوتبال در این فصل خوشحال شده است. آیکمن کمتر از حضور متوسط ​​آلما مادرش در بازی های خانگی در این فصل، که در طول پیروزی هفته گذشته در رتبه 8 برتر UdaC در رتبه 8-270، آشکار شد، ابراز نگرانی کرده است. ورزشگاه نمادین رز بول UCLA می تواند 90888 نفر را در خود جای دهد، اما تنها 24611 نفر برای هشتمین برد بروینز مقابل نوادا حضور داشتند. آیکمن اعتراف کرد که این موضوع در حین حضور در نمایش 96.7 «بلیت» دالاس در روز پنجشنبه او را عصبانی کرد. آیکمن در یک اعلامیه افتضاح گفت: «خجالت آور نیست که ما در بازی هفته گذشته 7-0 بودیم و آنها آن را بسیار پایین [در تلویزیون] نشان دادند، بنابراین شما واقعا نمی توانید تشخیص دهید که چه زمانی بازی را تماشا می کنید - به من گفته می شود که حدود 20 تا 25000 نفر در بازی حضور داشتند. 25000، ممکن است برخلاف برخی از ورزشگاه‌های دیگر که شاید 40000 استادیوم دارند خالی باشد. "ما باید مردم را به بازی‌ها تشویق کنیم، باید آنها را در مورد آن هیجان زده کنیم. و سپس می‌گویید، "خب، چگونه آنها را هیجان زده می‌کنید؟ اگر 7-0 آنها را هیجان زده نمی‌کند، چه خواهد شد؟" من پاسخ آن را نمی‌دانم."
24,611 تعداد هواداران قابل احترامی است که آیکمن به آن اشاره کرد. اما ورزشگاه رز بول باعث می شود 24,611 هوادار کوچک به نظر برسد، به خصوص برای یکی از بهترین تیم های فوتبال دانشگاهی کشور. با این وجود، بروین ها به پیشروی خود ادامه خواهند داد. آن‌ها در مینه‌سوتا در تشک بیگ تین بازی می‌کنند

It’s quite a week for new movies on VOD, with some of the biggest pictures of the year arriving to digital platforms. This week, you can catch Robert Pattinson in Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim film about the ethically questionable goings-on behind the scenes of Dateline‘s “To Catch A Predator,” and Zach Cregger’s comedic and gory interpretation of Resident Evil.

Also out this week is Musk, the Alex Gibney documentary that Elon Musk doesn’t want you to see, as well as the Mahershala Ali action thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. Need some feminine energy instead? Check out Lady, the mockumentary starring Fleabag‘s Sian Clifford as a narcissistic aristocrat who hires a film crew to follow her.

These are just a few of the films that are available to watch on Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, YouTube, and through your cable service this week. Check out what movies are available to buy or rent on demand now.

The latest film in the Resident Evil movie franchise was directed by Zach Cregger, who knocked it out of the park with his first two films, Barbarian and Weapons, and continues his hot streak with this latest release. The new film stars Austin Abrams as a medical courier named Bryan Hodukavich who ends up battling his way through a sea of infected, mutated people while on a delivery run in Raccoon City. Zach Cherry, Kalie Reis and Paul Walter Hauser also star.

Directed by documentary filmmaker Lance Oppenheim (who also co-directed the recently-released documentary You Can See Everything with Nathan Fielder) in his feature film debut, Primetime stars Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, the journalist who hosted NBC’s “To Catch a Predator” for Dateline NBC from 2004 to 2007, which involved luring alleged sexual predators who were purportedly seeking sex with a minor into a sting operation. The film arrived to digital platforms this week.

This subway performance got derailed in a hurry.

A former “American Idol” contestant held his ground after being “attacked” by a disgruntled straphanger and won over a car full of straphangers on the A train in Manhattan, a viral video showed.

Shane Dan Turner, 29, was busking between 125th Street and Columbus Circle Wednesday afternoon when a woman who claimed her ears were too sensitive for his music grabbed his tip money and drowned him out with her own loud wailing, according to the clip.

“That was me being attacked by a mentally ill woman,” Turner said as he reshared the clip with an explainer at the end of it.

The video starts with the woman seen tussling with Turner and pleading with other riders to “make him stop” playing, while sharing that she just “had surgery on my f–king ear.”

Another woman is heard jawing at the antagonizer to “get your ass off the train,” advising her to use “Access-a-Ride” because that she “shouldn’t be on the train” if she just had surgery.

As the two women traded vulgar barbs, Turner changed a broken guitar string and launched into “I Don’t Love You” by My Chemical Romance, a song he hoped would “piss [her] off and try to get [her] to leave,” for another train car as the A made the long express journey from Harlem to Midtown.

Undettered, the woman sang along at full volume, drowning out the career performer as previously disengaged straphangers became visibly amused.

“This woman has lungs that I couldn’t compete with without a microphone,” Turner said on his Instagram page.

“This woman’s complaining about an ear surgery and she’s screaming at the top of her lungs.”

The artist, who competed on Season 23 of “Idol” last year, said the only-in-New York encounter started when the woman tried to sing over him before commenting on a pin he was wearing that read “I’m autistic, awkwardness may occur.”

“She sees the pin and goes ‘you’re applauding an autistic guy, he’s probably just wearing that for marketing,'” Turner recounted.

When he told the woman that he was “actually autistic,” she replied “that’s disgusting and narcissistic,” and grabbed for tip money that was in his case, according to Turner.

By the end of the clip, Turner had clearly won over the other straphangers on the crowded car, earning loud applause, verbal encouragement and tips from his fellow New Yorkers.

“They were giving me tips in my hand because they knew this woman was trying to grab it from my tip case.”

The singer shared with his followers that he suffers from a litany of mental health problems, but believes that the woman who tried to rob him and stymie his performance was the one who needed treatment.

“I got nothing on this person,” Turner said.

“I just wish she gets the help she needs; she was probably just having a very bad day.”

موارد بیشتری از پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. این اجرای مترو با عجله از ریل خارج شد. یک ویدیوی ویروسی نشان داد که یک شرکت کننده سابق "American Idol" پس از "حمله" توسط یک مرد ناراضی ناراضی و غلبه بر خودرویی پر از straphangers در قطار A در منهتن، موضع خود را حفظ کرد. شین دن ترنر، 29 ساله، بعدازظهر چهارشنبه بین خیابان 125 و حلقه کلمبوس در حال تردد بود که زنی که ادعا می کرد گوش هایش برای موسیقی او خیلی حساس است، پول انعام او را گرفت و با ناله بلند خودش غرقش کرد. طبق این کلیپ، ترنر در پایان کلیپ با پخش مجدد آن گفت: "این بود که توسط یک زن بیمار روانی به من حمله شد." ویدئو با زنی شروع می شود که در حال درگیری با ترنر و التماس از دیگر سواران است تا "او را متوقف کند" در حال بازی، در حالی که به اشتراک می گذارد که او فقط "گوش f-king من را جراحی کرده است."

news.originalContent:
Christians in Indonesia face an underreported pattern of threats and protests as radical Islamists weaponize bureaucratic red tape to stop them from practicing their faith, even in private residences.

Though reporting is largely limited to citizen journalists and small Christian publications, a review of reported incidents reveals a tried-and-true method used to repress Christians in the world’s most populous Islamic nation, despite religious freedom being guaranteed by law. (RELATED: Faith Groups Warn Proposed Law Could Blind America To Christian Massacres)

While the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees “all persons the freedom of worship, each according to his/her own religion or belief,” heavy permitting requirements make it increasingly difficult for religious minorities to establish places of public worship. This gives hostile groups of Muslims an opportunity to stop Christians from practicing their faith.

Fredrik J. Pinakunary, chairman of the Supervisory Board of the Indonesian Christian Legal Society, told the Daily Caller that while established minority communities, such as Christians, Hindus, and Buddhists, remain relatively peaceful and secure, “friction typically flares around two specific flashpoints: applying for and constructing new places of worship, and holding non-routine religious gatherings outside registered sanctuaries—such as residential prayer meetings, or special holiday gatherings.”

For Christians, these flashpoints can leave them with two choices: apply for a permit and endure years of red tape while facing continual protests, or hold small worship and prayer services that risk being interrupted by threats of violence. Those threats often end in local meetings that let the person making them off the hook while the church is forced to suspend services.

A post shared by Derek VanBuskirk (@derek_vanbuskirk)

“If you don’t close it, bloodshed will occur inside,” a machete-wielding Muslim man, accompanied by a few others, said as he interrupted a prayer service involving approximately 40 Christians in late September, according to Morning Star News. “Yes, I am not afraid to die … For Allah, I am not afraid to die.”

As the congregants fled, the man continued, justifying his outrage by claiming the prayer rooms lacked permits and that he was part of “the majority.”

Despite the threats, the man was not immediately arrested. Instead, he met with community leaders, where he offered his “deepest apologies.” The meeting initially resulted in an agreement to take no legal action, but the settlement later collapsed after officials ordered the prayer house closed, according to Morning Star News.

In fact, Pinakunary said such attempts at mediation often “come at the expense of the minority congregation” as law enforcement and community leaders prioritize keeping the peace and avoiding violent clashes over protecting constitutional liberties.

A post shared by Derek VanBuskirk (@derek_vanbuskirk)

In another heated example, an Oct. 6 meeting with community leaders over six Christians worshipping in a private home ended with an official record mandating the suspension of services until all administrative requirements had been met. However, the meeting’s minutes did not specify which requirements remained incomplete, Persecution.org reported.

The pastor said he agreed to the deal only because he feared for his family’s and home’s safety. He added that one neighborhood leader struck a table and said, “Arrest them; if they resist, kill them,” according to Persecution.org.

These intimidation tactics are not new and stem from abuses of the requirements needed to structure a church, as stated in a 2006 Joint Ministerial Decree issued by the Ministers of Religious Affairs and Home Affairs, according to Pinakunary.

In perhaps the earliest example of this, Islamist protesters were able to stall a church’s creation for 15 years despite having met all of the decree’s requirements in 2006.

An Indonesian policeman stands guard outside a church after an explosion in Makassar on March 28, 2021. (Photo by INDRA ABRIYANTO/AFP via Getty Images)

These requirements include a list of at least 90 prospective congregants, verified by local authorities; written signatures of support from at least 60 neighbors living in the immediate vicinity, validated by the local village or neighborhood head; and a written recommendation from the local office of the Ministry of Religious Affairs and the local Religious Harmony Forum.

While Pinakunary said the joint decree was intended to promote religious harmony, it “quickly backfired” because the prerequisites, especially the 60-neighbor consent, “gave hostile neighbors an effective pocket veto, even when applicants met every other standard.”

This year, at least 11 places of worship have had construction halted after protests from groups alleging that permitting requirements were not met. The necessary paperwork had been completed in all but five cases. One church was raided for repairing its roof without a permit, and another spent the last nine years trying to secure one with no success. (RELATED: Pope Leo XIV Makes History As First Pope To Vote In US Election)

In one case, arson and subsequent attempts to redo the paperwork disrupted construction, while local officials rejected the revised applications. The church building has remained unfinished since breaking ground in 2004.

“Even a bulletproof application does not guarantee a church will ever be built,” Pinakunary told the Caller, adding that “even when a congregation checks every box and secures every formal permit, mob resistance frequently persists.”

A post shared by Christianity In Indonesia (@indonesianchristians)

In an early October protest, a video shows an Islamic leader addressing a crowd over a loudspeaker, claiming there were “many irregularities starting from the permits” and accusing the church of offering bribes.

“Be careful, servants of Allah. This Muslim community is already this incredibly angry,” the man continued, warning that the church would bring “chaos” to the community. He said residents feared their grandchildren would leave the faith and become polytheists.

The man added that if the church were built, they would wait for the opportune time to “dismantle” it.

A video taken Oct. 30 documented the latest demonstration against establishing a church. While security stood by, local leaders met to discuss the church’s fate.

David Herson, a religious liberty advocate in Indonesia, told the Caller the meeting was taking place despite the church having already secured the proper permits.

A post shared by KABAR MARGAASIH (@kabar_margaasih)

A March report from the Setara Institute found 3,823 incidents and 5,639 actions against freedom of religion and belief across Indonesia since 2007.

Pinakunary said those findings made clear that “religious intolerance is a real, persistent problem on the ground. Administrative technicalities like a ‘lack of permits’ are routinely weaponized to give religious suppression a veneer of legal legitimacy.”

While Herson affirmed that using permits to deny Christians the right to worship is indeed a pattern, he said it is not the only tool being used.

Pastor Dedi Saputra was sentenced to two years in prison in July for blasphemy and the dissemination of hate speech via social media. His alleged offense was sharing the Christian gospel on TikTok following his conversion from Islam, Persecution.org reported.

Pinakunary told the Caller that disputes and rights violations will continue unless structural legal reforms take place. He pointed to a dedicated Freedom of Religion Bill proposed by Human Rights Minister Natalius Pigai in 2026, which could “offer vital statutory protection for religious minorities across the country and provide teeth to Indonesia’s constitutional guarantees.” (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Nigerian Leaders Turn On Alleged ‘Christian-Killing’ Warlord After U.S. Pressure According To Whistleblower)

“Indonesia belongs to all of us,” Herson told the Caller. “No one should be intimidated, discriminated against, or prevented from exercising their constitutional right to worship. Whether someone is Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, Catholic, or belongs to another faith, everyone deserves the same respect, protection, and freedom.”

Treveyon Henderson is dealing with a medical emergency, the Patriots’ star running back revealed in a social media post on Friday morning.

After he missed last week’s game with what was described as an illness, the situation has lingered for more than a week and will likely cost him this Sunday’s matchup with the Packers.

Henderson described his battle as an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency” involving a series of “unexplained” neurological symptoms.

“Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days. During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable,” Henderson said in a statement.

“I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health.”

Henderson led the Patriots in total offensive yards last season as an explosive ball carrier and receiving threat, helping lead the team to a Super Bowl berth.

The Patriots selected him in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft and it was expected that he would usurp Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s starter, though that has not yet come to fruition.

“My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities,” Henderson added.

Henderson then explained that his wife and and religion has helped get him through this difficult time.

“I want to thank my wife for being by my side throughout all of this, and most importantly, I want to thank Jesus for giving me a peace that surpasses all understanding. Despite all of this, my heart rejoices in The Lord and my heart is at peace knowing that He is always faithful and His promise of Romans 8:28 always remain true,” Henderson wrote.

“And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose. The purpose of trials in life is not to drive us away from God, but to only bring us closer. May God’s Will be done, not mine. My wife and I are deeply grateful for family and loved ones, the New England Patriots organization, my agent, my medical team, teammates, and everyone who has offered prayers, encouragement, and support. We respectfully ask for continued prayers and privacy as we focus on my health and recovery.”

The Patriots have utilized Corey Kiner as the second string to Stevenson, but their run game remains lackluster at best without Henderson in the fold.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. تریویون هندرسون با یک اورژانس پزشکی دست و پنجه نرم می کند، ستاره دونده میهن پرستان در یک پست رسانه اجتماعی در صبح روز جمعه فاش کرد. پس از اینکه او بازی هفته گذشته را به دلیل بیماری که به عنوان یک بیماری توصیف شد از دست داد، این وضعیت برای بیش از یک هفته باقی مانده است و احتمالاً به قیمت بازی یکشنبه با پکرز تمام خواهد شد. هندرسون نبرد خود را به عنوان یک "اورژانس پزشکی غیرمنتظره و غیرمعمول" با مجموعه ای از علائم عصبی "غیرقابل توضیح" توصیف کرد. "اخیراً، من یک اورژانس پزشکی غیرمنتظره و غیرمعمول را تجربه کردم که شامل یک سری علائم عصبی غیرقابل توضیح بود که نیاز به بستری شدن در بیمارستان برای چند روز داشت. در طی آن مدت، تحت آزمایش و ارزیابی پزشکی گسترده قرار گرفتم. هندرسون در بیانیه‌ای گفت: در حالی که نتایج آزمایش‌های پزشکی جامع من مثبت و اطمینان‌بخش است، علت این امر ناشناخته و غیرقابل توضیح است. من متعهد به انجام هر کاری لازم برای بازگشت به سلامت کامل هستم.» هندرسون فصل گذشته در مجموع یاردهای تهاجمی پاتریوتز را به عنوان یک حامل توپ انفجاری هدایت کرد و تهدیدی را دریافت کرد و به هدایت تیم به جایگاه سوپربول کمک کرد.

Jen Affleck’s divorce from Zac Affleck took a bitter turn after she posted a video of him criticizing her postpartum body — after he claimed to be her biggest supporter.

On Thursday, Zac posted a TikTok video breaking his silence on the split, in which he confirmed that he learned she filed for divorce on the news. He also noted that despite the split, he will continue to be her “biggest fan.”

Following his emotional upload, Jen took to her own TikTok page and shared a throwback video where she was two weeks postpartum and he warned her not to post a video showing her “sagging tits.”

In the footage, Zac, 30, could be heard saying, “[I] hope you’re not making a TikTok looking like that. … Your boobs are literally like … Your tits are sagging all over. You don’t want to post that, baby, I can tell you that right now.”

“He was never my biggest supporter,” Jen, 27, captioned the post, directly referring to her estranged husband’s post.

A follower called out Zac about Jen’s upload in the comments section of his video on Thursday, writing, “As much as I don’t like Jen.. if my husband told me my boobs were ‘saggy’ 2 weeks after giving birth, I’d never forgive him.”

Zac responded, “This was a video from 2022. Obviously horrible and should have never been said. When I saw the video today, I was absolutely shocked I had said that. I said a lot of horrible and hurtful things, but I have tried my best to learn and grow.”

The “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star took another swipe at Zac by posting an additional video of a tense moment during their marriage where he seemed to scold her for not putting a dirty towel away.

“I’ve been all your laundry for the past… forever,” Jen told him. “If I got a little bit more help from you it would be nice. Maybe we’d have some towels.”

In turn, Zac walked away angrily.

Zac admitted to making “plenty of mistakes” in their marriage in his Thursday video.

“I don’t want anyone speaking bad about Jen,” he told his followers. “I’ll be the first to say I’ve made plenty of mistakes in our marriage, and it just really was time for us to go our own ways. We got married so young, and it sucks because I really did feel like we had something pretty special when we got married.”

On Wednesday, Page Six confirmed that Jen submitted her divorce filing Tuesday in Utah County District Court, as well as a parenting plan.

Jen and Zac share three children — Nora, 4, Lucas, 3, and Penelope, 1 — and she is currently pregnant with their fourth child.

As their split made headlines, the parents separately celebrated their eldest child’s birthday on Wednesday.

بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. طلاق جن افلک از زک افلک بعد از انتشار ویدئویی از او در انتقاد از بدن پس از زایمانش - بعد از اینکه ادعا کرد بزرگترین حامی او است، طلاق تلخی گرفت. روز پنجشنبه، زک ویدیویی از TikTok منتشر کرد که سکوت خود را در مورد جدایی شکسته بود، که در آن تایید کرد که از خبر طلاق خود مطلع شده است. او همچنین خاطرنشان کرد که با وجود این جدایی، او همچنان "بزرگترین طرفدار او" خواهد بود. پس از بارگذاری احساسی خود، جن به صفحه خود در TikTok رفت و یک ویدیوی بازگشتی را به اشتراک گذاشت که در آن دو هفته پس از زایمان بود و به او هشدار داد که ویدیویی را که نشان دهنده «افتادگی سینه‌هایش» است، منتشر نکند.
در این فیلم، صدای زک 30 ساله شنیده می‌شود که می‌گوید: "امیدوارم شما یک TikTok اینطوری درست نکنید... سینه‌های شما به معنای واقعی کلمه شبیه هستند... سینه‌هایتان در همه جا آویزان شده‌اند. شما نمی‌خواهید آن را پست کنید، عزیزم، می‌توانم همین الان به شما بگویم." جن، 27 ساله، با اشاره مستقیم به پست شوهرش که از همسرش جدا شده بود، در توضیح این پست نوشت: "او هرگز بزرگترین حامی من نبود."
زک پاسخ داد: «این یک ویدیو از سال 2022 بود. بدیهی است که وحشتناک است و هرگز نباید گفته می شد. وقتی امروز ویدیو را دیدم، کاملاً شوکه شدم که این را گفتم. من چیزهای وحشتناک و آزاردهنده زیادی گفتم، اما تمام تلاشم را کرده ام که یاد بگیرم و رشد کنم.»

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

By the end of 2026, a record-setting 21.7 million Americans will have set sail on a cruise. While the masses continue to demonstrate their deep love for maritime adventure, some are behaving below board while onboard.

To determine decency and all that falls beyond it, leading experts recently revealed the rudest things a cruise passenger can do.

The primary discourtesy? Monopolizing pool loungers.

Cruise passengers have long followed a tradition of grabbing anything they can find — towels, flip-flops, even dolls — to reserve pool lounge chairs for hours.

“Reserving a pool lounger for while you’re off enjoying another activity is simply unfair,” Deborah Director, a SmartFlyer travel advisor, told Travel + Leisure.

“Everyone deserves an opportunity to enjoy the ship’s amenities, particularly when outdoor space is at a premium.”

Many cruise lines are doing their part to curb the behavior.

Royal Caribbean has a strict policy stating that pool deck chairs are available on a first-come, first-served basis and cannot be reserved.

Last year, passengers praised Norwegian Cruise Line for enforcing its anti-chair-hogging policy.

According to reports, crew members actively marked unoccupied chairs with stickers, and if sunbathers didn’t return within an hour, they removed towels and personal items from the unattended loungers.

T+L also called out cruisers who don’t utilize the handwashing stations by the buffets, as going sans soap greatly increases the risk of contracting and spreading illnesses onboard.

This May, a Princess Cruises ship was rocked by a norovirus outbreak that affected more than 100 passengers and 20 crew.

Norovirus is the most common cause of gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships, according to the CDC. It accounted for 17 of the 23 CDC-reported cruise ship outbreaks last year.

As one Reddit user surmised, “Lack of hand hygiene is my biggest ick. The ships make it so easy for everyone to wash their hands. It helps reduce the spread of illness. Cruise ships don’t have to be floating petri dishes.”

Silence is one sound you’re unlikely to enjoy on a cruise ship.

On a Reddit thread, a first-time cruiser counted loudness as her primary complaint.

“The noise was pretty overwhelming on my first cruise this winter. I wore earplugs a lot of the time. Noisy people in the hallways at all hours. I lost a lot of sleep.

Experts note that some of the most offensive sound sources are personal speakers.

While Carnival prohibits portable speakers, others like Virgin Voyages and MSC Cruises restrict them to staterooms.

Many cruisers report passengers pushing into an elevator before others have exited, causing chaos, discomfort, and unnecessary congestion.

“It’s not only rude, but it also doesn’t even gain them anything,” said a puzzled Reddit user, “Not even a quicker arrival at their deck of choice, since the traffic jam at the door only delays the departure of the lift.”

Experts note that the petty practice is particularly inconsiderate to older travelers and people with disabilities.

A legion of cruisers say they take the stairs to avoid this trash behavior and burn extra calories.

T+L notes that rude cruisers routinely clutter corridors with their used dishes and room service trays, which, as dangerous as it is disgusting, can obstruct pathways.

Experts underscore the importance of calling room service to request pickup as soon as you have finished your in-room meal.

Others have noticed the plate problem both outside of rooms and in the dining room itself.

“People do this weird thing on cruises where they’ll put their dirty plates on other people’s tables while still in use to clear up a table. Don’t do this. I can’t stand someone putting their dirty dishes on my table while I’m still eating. I’ve never seen this happen anywhere other than cruises,” reported one Reddit user.

Being rude to the crew resounds through Reddit as a primary pet peeve.

“These people are paid to cater to your every wish. The least you can do is be polite to them,” said one user.

According to Calderwood, passenger conflicts usually trace back to poor preparation and surprise over vessel rules.

While booking shows, dining, and excursions early prevents headaches, frustration never excuses berating, belittling, or otherwise mistreating crew members.
news.content: پوشش های بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. تا پایان سال 2026، رکورد 21.7 میلیون آمریکایی به یک کشتی دریایی سفر خواهند کرد. در حالی که توده‌ها همچنان عشق عمیق خود را به ماجراجویی دریایی نشان می‌دهند، برخی در حین سوار شدن در زیر کشتی رفتار می‌کنند. برای تعیین نجابت و همه چیزهایی که فراتر از آن است، کارشناسان برجسته اخیراً بی‌رحمانه‌ترین کارهایی را که یک مسافر کروز می‌تواند انجام دهد فاش کرده‌اند. بی ادبی اصلی؟ انحصار صندلی های استخر. مسافران کروز مدت‌هاست که از سنت برداشتن هر چیزی که پیدا می‌کنند - حوله، دمپایی، حتی عروسک - برای رزرو صندلی‌های استخر برای ساعت‌ها پیروی می‌کنند. دبورا مدیر، مشاور سفر SmartFlyer، به Travelery + Evone Leisures گفت: «رزرو صندلی استخر برای زمانی که از فعالیت دیگری لذت می‌برید، به سادگی ناعادلانه است. به خصوص زمانی که فضای بیرونی از قیمت بالایی برخوردار است.» بسیاری از خطوط کروز سهم خود را برای مهار این رفتار انجام می‌دهند. رویال کارائیب یک سیاست سختگیرانه دارد مبنی بر اینکه صندلی‌های عرشه استخر بر اساس اولویت در دسترس هستند و نمی‌توان آنها را رزرو کرد. سال گذشته، مسافران خط کروز نروژی را به دلیل اعمال سیاست‌های ضد هولینگ صندلی تحسین کردند. بر اساس گزارش‌ها، اعضای خدمه به طور فعال صندلی‌های خالی را با برچسب علامت‌گذاری می‌کردند و اگر آفتاب‌گیران ظرف یک ساعت برنمی‌گشتند، حوله‌ها و وسایل شخصی را از صندلی‌های بدون مراقبت خارج می‌کردند. T+L همچنین رزمناوهایی را که از ایستگاه‌های شستشوی دست در بوفه استفاده نمی‌کردند، نامید و آنها را بی‌نظیر خواند.

Amateur cricketer caught clicking his fingers while fielding to trick umpire into thinking the batsman had edged the ball.

The English amateur cricketer who went viral ⁠for finger-clicking trickery ⁠has been handed a two-year suspension, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League has said.

The fielder Brian Devine, dubbed “Clicky Ponting” on ⁠social media in a nod to former Australia captain Ricky Ponting, was accused of tricking umpires by clicking his fingers to make the ⁠sound of a ball nicking the bat as deliveries were missed and caught by the wicketkeeper.

The video footage went viral on social media and made international headlines earlier this year. A three-person disciplinary panel reviewed the ‌footage and considered player interviews and written statements before imposing the ban.

“The player concerned is suspended from all cricket under the ECB’s [the England and Wales Cricket Board] jurisdiction for two years, from 30 September 2026 to 29 September 2028. This covers playing, coaching, umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams,” the NYSDL said in a statement on Friday.

Additionally, Saltburn ⁠Cricket Club have been fined 300 pounds ($402.87) and ⁠their second XI has been relegated to Division Three of the NYSDCL and will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction, the league added.

Devine and Saltburn admitted the charges, but the club appealed against their sanction.

Saltburn said in a statement reported on gazettelive.co.uk: “The club fully participated in the disciplinary proceedings and accept the decision of the appeal following the original decision from the league.”

In a statement to the Press Association, the league said, “The league recognises the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person.

“We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete. The league will make no further comment.”

Ricky Ponting, who led Australia to two 50-over World Cup titles, told the Reuters news agency that he found ⁠the controversy amusing, although he was less ⁠impressed that his name had become associated with the player.

“I had a bit of a chuckle to myself and pretty much forgot about it after that,” he said in an ‌interview earlier this year.

“I guess it wasn’t a nice thing to have my name associated with someone who’s blatantly cheating but … honestly I ‌had ‌a laugh and a joke about it.”

news.originalContent:
Evicted families take Denmark’s controversial ‘ghetto law’ to the Supreme Court.

Seven families from Helsingor, a coastal city north of Copenhagen, are facing their former landlord in Denmark’s Supreme Court.

In a two-day hearing that began on Friday, they are arguing they were forced from their homes because of where they, or their parents, come from.

Their leases were terminated in 2022 under a 2018 law, once known as the “ghetto law”, which targets social housing estates where more than half of residents are classed as “non-Western”. The government claims the law is aimed at integration. But rights groups have for years fought against the measures, saying they are discriminatory.

“It’s about whether the criteria regarding the tenants’ origin is neutral or not,” Eddie Khawaja, the families’ lawyer, told the news agency AFP.

So what does “non-Western” mean, and could the courts bring the law down? Here’s what you need to know:

It is a statistical label that covers most of the world.

In 2020, the UN Human Rights Office said: “Statistics Denmark, under the Danish Ministry for Economic and Interior Affairs, defines ‘non-Western’ as any country outside the EU, with the exceptions of Andorra, Australia, Canada, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, New Zealand, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, the USA, and the Vatican State.

“The effect is that ‘non-Western’ disproportionately means Denmark’s non-white, non-European ethnic populations,” it stated.
The label also covers descendants: anyone born in Denmark if neither parent is a Danish citizen born in the country.

That means a Danish citizen born and raised in Copenhagen can still be “non-Western”.

Every December 1, the government names “parallel societies”.

These are social housing areas of at least 1,000 people where more than 50 percent are “non-Western” immigrants and descendants.

An area must also meet two of four criteria on unemployment, crime, education, and income.

Areas on the list for five years become “transformation areas”, which the government used to call “hard ghettos”.

They must cut public family housing to 40 percent by 2030 through sales, demolition or conversion.

An estate with the same social problems but fewer “non-Western” residents faces no such obligation.

The government says the goal is integration.

The law was part of a plan called “One Denmark without Parallel Societies: No Ghettos in 2030”.

In 2021, Kaare Dybvad Bek, then interior minister, said too many non-Western foreigners in one area “increases the risk of an emergence of religious and cultural parallel societies”.

About 11,000 people across Denmark will have to leave their homes by 2030, according to tenants’ associations.

In Helsingor, the landlord Boliggarden announced in early 2020 that it would renovate 96 apartments at the Nojsomhed estate. It then terminated the tenants’ leases. Most of those tenants were of foreign origin.

“They didn’t want the estate to be labelled ‘hard ghetto’ so they wanted to forcibly move us out when we advocated for other solutions,” Riad, a 33-year-old plaintiff who did not want his family name published, told AFP.

The law may be discriminatory, but Danish judges ultimately make the final decision about whether it violated Danish laws prohibiting ethnic discrimination.

The Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) ruled in December 2025, in cases brought by tenants from Mjolnerparken in Copenhagen and Schackenborgvaenge in Slagelse. It said nationality or country of birth alone does not determine ethnic origin, but an allegedly neutral criterion covering many origins could be linked to ethnicity.

That runs contrary to the Danish government’s position and the reasoning of the lower Danish courts in the Helsingor case, which found that the “non-Western” does not describe an ethnic group and therefore did not result in discrimination that violated Denmark’s Equal Treatment Act.

Danish judges must decide whether the “non-Western” criterion really rests on residents’ ethnic origin, the court said, and consequently, if people included in the criterion are afforded less favourable treatment.

Less favourable treatment, it noted, could include “an increased risk of early termination of their leases”.

In January, Sophie Haestorp Andersen, then minister for social affairs and housing, told a parliamentary hearing that authorities must keep applying the law until the Eastern High Court rules, the Danish outlet Danske Kommuner reported.

The four-party coalition in power since June includes the Green Left (SF), which voted for the law in 2018, according to the public broadcaster DR. The party’s Jacob Mark is now minister for children, elderly affairs and housing.

No date has been officially set for the verdict, but reports suggest it could be handed down later this month.

If the families win, they would probably be rehoused in homes similar to the ones they had to leave.

The Mjolnerparken case is still before the Eastern High Court.
news.content:
خانواده‌های اخراج‌شده «قانون گتو» بحث‌برانگیز دانمارک را به دادگاه عالی می‌برند. هفت خانواده از هلسینگور، شهری ساحلی در شمال کپنهاگ، با صاحبخانه سابق خود در دادگاه عالی دانمارک روبرو هستند. در یک جلسه دو روزه که از روز جمعه آغاز شد، آنها استدلال می‌کنند که به خاطر جایی که از خانه یا والدینشان آمده‌اند مجبور به ترک خانه‌هایشان شده‌اند. قراردادهای اجاره آنها در سال 2022 بر اساس قانون سال 2018، که زمانی به عنوان "قانون محله یهودی نشین" شناخته می شد، فسخ شد، که املاک مسکونی اجتماعی را هدف قرار می دهد که بیش از نیمی از ساکنان آن به عنوان "غیر غربی" طبقه بندی می شوند. دولت مدعی است هدف این قانون یکپارچه سازی است. اما گروه‌های حقوق بشر سال‌ها با این اقدامات مبارزه کرده و می‌گویند که این اقدامات تبعیض‌آمیز است. ادی خواجه، وکیل خانواده ها، به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت: «مسئله این است که آیا معیارهای مربوط به منشاء مستاجران بی طرف است یا نه. در اینجا چیزی است که باید بدانید:
این یک برچسب آماری است که بیشتر نقاط جهان را پوشش می دهد. در سال 2020، دفتر حقوق بشر سازمان ملل متحد گفت: «آمار دانمارک، زیر نظر وزارت امور اقتصادی و کشور دانمارک، «غیر غربی» را به عنوان هر کشوری خارج از اتحادیه اروپا، به استثنای آندورا، استرالیا، کانادا، ایسلند، لیختن اشتاین، موناکو، نیوزیلند، نروژ، سن ماریلو، ایالت واتیک، ایالات متحده آمریکا، تعریف می کند. در این بیانیه آمده است: «اثر این است که «غیر غربی» به طور نامتناسبی به معنای جمعیت‌های قومی غیر سفیدپوست و غیر اروپایی دانمارک است.

news.originalContent:
Released in 2023, the truck has become a symbol to some of opposition to Musk amid foray into US politics.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has said the company will wind down production of Cybertrucks at its Texas facility amid poor sales.

Trillionaire Musk made the announcement in a post on X on Friday, saying the wind-down would enable the company to increase its production of the new Cybercab model, launched as part of a foray into the so-called robo-taxi industry.

“Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production,” Musk wrote.

Announced in 2019, the Cybertruck’s stark design, featuring an angular stainless steel exterior, proved immediately polarising.

At an unveiling ceremony that year, Musk sought to prove its windows were shatterproof. But the exhibition backfired, with metal balls launched at the car cracking two of the windows.

The vehicle quickly became a symbol of opposition to Musk as he became increasingly involved in United States politics, including briefly leading the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) panel tasked by the administration of US President Donald Trump with cleaving federal government agencies.

Musk most recently spent nearly half a billion dollars in the US midterm election campaign in support of Republican candidates, including more than $200 million in support of the failed Senate candidacy of Republican Ken Paxton in Texas. Beyond Tesla, Musk’s SpaceX company is also based in Texas.

But the spending did little to prevent a blue wave in US politics, which saw Democrats take commanding control of the US House of Representatives and Senate. The shift could spell investigations into Musk’s work with the federal government.

Musk had initially predicted the Cybertrucks, which became available to consumers at the end of 2023, would sell at a rate of about 250,000 a year.

The model fell far below that target. In 2024, about 38,965 units were sold. That figure declined by nearly half in 2025, with 20,237 sold.

In his announcement on Friday, Musk did not say whether Cybertruck manufacturing would shift to another factory. The plant in Texas is the only known production site.

In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the “best vehicle Tesla has ever made”, hailing the “end of an era”.
news.content: این کامیون که در سال 2023 عرضه شد، به نمادی برای برخی از مخالفان ماسک در بحبوحه ورود به سیاست ایالات متحده تبدیل شد. ایلان ماسک، مدیر عامل تسلا، گفته است که این شرکت در بحبوحه فروش ضعیف، تولید سایبرتراک در تاسیسات تگزاس خود را متوقف خواهد کرد. تریلیونر ماسک در روز جمعه در پستی در روز X اعلام کرد و گفت که این تعطیلی شرکت را قادر می‌سازد تا تولید مدل جدید Cybercab را افزایش دهد، که به عنوان بخشی از تلاش برای به اصطلاح صنعت تاکسی‌های رباتیک راه اندازی شده است. «تسلا در اواسط سال آینده تولید Cybertruck را در Gigafactory تگزاس به پایان می‌رساند. طراحی واضح Cybertruck که در سال 2019 معرفی شد، با نمای بیرونی از فولاد ضد زنگ زاویه‌دار، فوراً قطبی شد. ماسک در مراسم رونمایی آن سال تلاش کرد ثابت کند که شیشه‌های آن نشکن هستند. اما نمایشگاه نتیجه معکوس داشت و توپ‌های فلزی که به سمت خودرو پرتاب می‌شدند، دو تا از شیشه‌ها را شکستند. این وسیله نقلیه به سرعت به نمادی از مخالفت با ماسک تبدیل شد، زیرا او به طور فزاینده ای در سیاست ایالات متحده درگیر شد، از جمله رهبری مختصر پنل وزارت کارایی دولت (DOGE) که توسط دولت دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور ایالات متحده ماموریت داده شده بود تا آژانس های دولتی فدرال را جدا کند. ماسک اخیراً نزدیک به نیم میلیارد دلار در مبارزات انتخاباتی میان دوره ای ایالات متحده برای حمایت از نامزدهای جمهوری خواه خرج کرد که از جمله آن بیش از 200 میلیون دلار برای حمایت از نامزدی ناموفق کن پکستون جمهوری خواه در تگزاس در سنا بود. فراتر از تسلا

news.originalContent:
A string of hoax alerts causing flight diversions across Europe this week have broadened to include newsrooms.

A new series of bomb threats caused more flight diversions across Europe on Friday, while also expanding to target a number of media organisations.

British broadcaster Sky said it was one of a number of newsrooms that received a bomb threat. “We have carried out a security assessment and reported the matter to the relevant authorities,” a spokesperson said.

Bulgaria’s Nova TV and the Irish public broadcaster RTE received emailed bomb threats from a purported “Mikhail Andropov”, headlined “Message to the West”, portraying the threats as a prelude to more disruptions across Europe.

RTE briefly evacuated staff, including radio and television presenters, in Dublin after an email was received on Friday morning. RTE Radio One presenter David McCullagh later told listeners that the threat warned that a bomb would explode within 45 minutes.

The Irish government said hoax bomb claims were also sent to Virgin Media, Newstalk radio and The Irish Independent newspaper and that it was unclear who was behind them.

“However, these threats come on the heels of the ongoing disruption to aviation around Europe caused by similar threats, and it seems likely that this is a coordinated campaign of disruption,” it said in a statement.

The incidents come a day after hoax bomb threats disrupted more than two dozen flights across Europe on Thursday, and days after other aircraft and a cruise ship received bomb alerts.

On Friday, jets escorted airliners flying from Brussels to Sofia and from Prague to Bucharest and Cyprus through Hungarian airspace due to bomb threats, Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said.

He also said NATO had ordered an air patrol near the Hungarian-Romanian border, the first report that the Western defence alliance had become involved.

Danish police said threats were directed at traffic at Copenhagen airport but that there appeared to be no danger to passengers. The airport said it was “operating normally”.

Czech police registered bomb threats to nine flights departing from or arriving in Prague. An airport spokesperson said no flights had been ⁠⁠cancelled as a result.

France said four new bomb threats were made to aircraft flying over French territory, and that all landed safely.

A Ryanair flight from Rome landed as scheduled in Lisbon, CNN Portugal reported.

About half a dozen ‌‌flights were disrupted on Tuesday and more than two dozen on Thursday, some of them making unplanned landings or being escorted to their destinations by fighter jets.

Al Jazeera’s Frances Read, reporting from London on Friday, said that while the threats have not been credible so far, disruptions appear to be widening.

“The number of hoax threats this week is making governments sit up and take notice about where this might be coming from and also think of solutions for how to deal with it,” she said.
news.content: مجموعه ای از هشدارهای دروغین که باعث انحراف پروازها در سراسر اروپا در این هفته می شود، به اتاق های خبر نیز گسترش یافته است. مجموعه جدیدی از تهدیدات بمب گذاری باعث انحراف بیشتر پروازها در سراسر اروپا در روز جمعه شد، در حالی که به هدف قرار دادن تعدادی از سازمان های رسانه ای نیز گسترش یافت. پخش کننده انگلیسی Sky گفت که این یکی از تعدادی اتاق خبری بود که تهدید بمب گذاری دریافت کرد.  یک سخنگوی گفت: «ما یک ارزیابی امنیتی انجام داده‌ایم و موضوع را به مقامات مربوطه گزارش کرده‌ایم. تلویزیون نوا بلغارستان و رادیو تلویزیون عمومی ایرلند RTE تهدیدات بمب‌گذاری شده را از طریق ایمیل ادعایی «میخائیل آندروپوف» با عنوان «پیام به غرب» دریافت کردند که این تهدیدها را مقدمه‌ای برای اختلالات بیشتر در سراسر اروپا نشان می‌داد. RTE برای مدت کوتاهی کارکنان از جمله مجریان رادیو و تلویزیون را در دوبلین پس از دریافت ایمیلی در صبح جمعه تخلیه کرد. دیوید مک‌کالا، مجری رادیو یک RTE بعداً به شنوندگان گفت که تهدید هشدار می‌دهد که یک بمب ظرف 45 دقیقه منفجر خواهد شد. دولت ایرلند گفت که ادعاهای دروغین بمب به ویرجین مدیا، رادیو Newstalk و روزنامه ایرلندی ایندیپندنت نیز ارسال شده است و مشخص نیست چه کسی پشت آنها بوده است. این سازمان در بیانیه ای اعلام کرد: «با این حال، این تهدیدها به دنبال اختلال مداوم در حمل و نقل هوایی در سراسر اروپا ناشی از تهدیدهای مشابه است، و به نظر می رسد که این یک کارزار هماهنگ اختلال است.» این حوادث یک روز پس از آن رخ می دهد که تهدیدات بمب جعلی باعث اختلال در بیش از دوجین پرواز در سراسر اروپا در روز پنجشنبه شد، و چند روز پس از هواپیماهای دیگر و یک هواپیمای دیگر.

news.originalContent:
A woman who claimed that men were being violently assaulted in a house for evading the draft has been arrested.

Petropavlivska-Borshchagivka, Ukraine – A woman wearing a crisp new paramedic’s uniform and impeccable makeup kneels on the ground in front of several police officers guarding the rusty gates of a two-storey house.

She begs, yells and curses, claiming that forcibly conscripted men are being held in the building in the tranquil suburb of Petropavlivska-Borshchagivka, outside the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv.

One of the men has already died, claims the woman, who was later identified as Valentyna Moloda, a 49-year-old nurse who once worked at a plastic surgery clinic and has never been authorised to practise as a paramedic.

The ambulance she arrived in carries the logos of a private medical company that reportedly stopped operating in 2023. A woman from Moloda’s “ambulance team” livestreams the scene as a crowd swells, joining in her chants demanding access to what she calls a “torture chamber.”

“I’m on my knees, let me get to them,” Moloda screams, claiming that “armed people” allegedly “torture” 40 people inside who had evaded the draft.

Her claims resonate with people at the impromptu rally, in a country where conscription officers have become reviled public servants due to their sometimes brutal tactics.

Protesters lob eggs at police and throw tomatoes at the house. The crowd grows to 500 people, with many clashing with officers until midnight.

Officials say that Moloda’s “rescue mission” on Monday afternoon – one of the most polarising scandals in Ukraine – was fake and required preparation.

But it had already gone viral online, with tens of thousands of people around the world lamenting Ukraine’s handling of conscription.

Glenn Diesen, a pro-Kremlin political analyst from Norway, shared a video and a photo on X of a teenager who fell while trying to film the house from the fence, claiming the boy was a victim of “great outrage and riots in Ukraine against the henchmen of [Ukrainian President Volodymyr] Zelenskyy and NATO.” His post has been widely shared.

Three days before Monday’s incident, Moloda and her driver “conducted a reconnaissance” of the house, Ukraine’s Chief of Staff Kyrylo Budanov said on Tuesday.

A former top military intelligence officer and one of Ukraine’s most popular and trusted public figures, Budanov interacted with Moloda at the time of the standoff.

Several young men clashed with police and tried to kick the doors of the house open until officers let Moloda and her team inside.

She came back minutes later to proclaim that she had just seen a man on the brink of death, another with a broken spine and one who was so badly beaten he was unable to talk.

“There’s blood on the mattresses,” she yelled, showing someone photos of the alleged victims on her phone, while the scene was livestreamed. “They [urinate] in a bottle.”

But careful observers would have noticed the videos were tagged as having been shot on Saturday. The crowd, however, kept growing, damaging police cars and clashing with officers.

Budanov arrived about six hours after Moloda started her livestream, and said that the besieged house on Solnichna Street had been used by the Azov Brigade, a former volunteer militia group of far-right nationalists and football fans that helped repel pro-Russian separatists in southeastern Ukraine in 2014.

Azov said apprehended deserters were kept in the house, while Azov’s commander Denys Prokopenko called the scandal a “sabotage behind the lines that discredits Ukrainian servicemen and creates a narrative that benefits Russia”.

The group has been accused of neo-Nazi sympathies and torturing war prisoners. The United States Department of State banned it from using US-supplied weaponry between 2014 and 2024, but it grew into a military force and became part of Ukraine’s National Guard. Its founder, Andriy Biletsky, led this year’s “Operation Vivaldi” to push Russian forces out of several strategic areas in eastern Ukraine.

After Budanov’s arrival, four men were allowed to walk out of the house into a bus, including the one Moloda claimed could not move because of a broken spine. The angry crowd did not allow the bus to leave.

Al Jazeera visited Petropavlivska-Borshchagivka and talked to more than a dozen residents, who insisted on full or partial anonymity because Monday’s scandal has become so politicised.

“Both sides are wrong,” an elderly man who only gave his first name, Serhiy, told Al Jazeera, standing next to his wife outside a supermarket.

“Azov shouldn’t have kept their people there, and the fake doctor shouldn’t have started all this noise,” he said.

His wife signalled him to stop talking and ushered him away.

Locals laughed off comparisons some have made between Monday’s incident and the massive 2013-2014 protests on Maidan Square in central Kyiv that toppled pro-Russian Ukrainian President Viktor Yanykovych.

“This definitely wasn’t a mini-Maidan,” 17-year-old Mykola told Al Jazeera, a short distance from the house. “Unfortunately, people believed that woman and flocked here.”

Most of the locals called the incident a “provocation”.

Only one man in his 30s said that Moloda “tried to help” and should not have been apprehended on Tuesday.

Moloda was arrested and is being held in custody for 60 days without bail.

Prosecutors said they found evidence proving that she had at least once carried out “rescue services” as a fake paramedic for 107,000 hryvnia ($2,355).

The relatives of a deserter, Andriy Kuleshov, allegedly hired Moloda for about $7,000 to get him out of the Azov house, Pavlo Kurchenko, a senior Azov officer, told the media outlet Ukrainska Pravda.

Kuleshov is listed in Myrotvorets – Ukrainian for “peacemaker” – a controversial online database of alleged anti-Ukrainian figures, for crossing into separatist-controlled areas in southeastern Ukraine multiple times in 2015-2021, where his brother lives.

“[Moloda] wanted to create a political scandal,” Volodymyr Fesenko, head of the Kyiv-based Penta think tank, told Al Jazeera. “She is also suspected of ties to Russian intelligence. So far, there’s no confirmation of that, but Russia has used this scandal in its interests.”

It did – with the help of pro-Russia Ukrainians.

“People are being kidnapped and tortured. Some are sold to military units, others – to their relatives. The weaker ones simply die of torture and confinement conditions,” Artyom Dmitruk, a former Ukrainian lawmaker with a pro-Russian party who fled for Italy in 2024, said in televised remarks.

The scandal “answers the question about why Russia needs the special military operation, to uproot the resurgent neo-Nazism in Ukraine,” said Mikhail Sheremev, a “lawmaker” in Russia-annexed Crimea.

Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion prompted a wave of volunteers to join Ukraine’s military, with tens of thousands enlisting across the country, often travelling to other regions because conscription offices near their homes were overwhelmed.

But after heavy losses and reports of poor planning, corruption and the cruelty of some officers, the number of volunteers fell dramatically.

Since 2023, conscription officers have been combing public places in search of people trying to avoid the draft. They have frequently forced them into their vans, often resorting to intimidation, beatings and torture, as Al Jazeera has reported, along with witnesses and human rights groups.

The officers claim there is no other way to mobilise the tens of thousands of men needed on the frontline to repel Russian forces.

The violence has led to corrupt practices.

As of August this year, 76 conscription officers had been arrested for accepting bribes of up to tens of thousands of dollars, stashing huge sums, and buying expensive properties in Ukraine and abroad.

Some draft-dodgers have secured fake exemptions from medical doctors, while others fled to neighbouring countries, either through bribes or by crossing the border without documentation.

Some forcibly drafted men secured the services of “fake ambulances”, according to prosecutors and police.

In 2025, border guards in the southwestern region of Zakarpattia detained a fake ambulance crew of three men who tried to take a person evading the draft to Romania for $10,000.

Below is State of the Day, a morning newsletter from the Daily Caller Editorial Desk. Sign up here.__________

Welcome to State of the Day,

How Americans soured on Big Tech’s favorite concrete boxes,

The Biggest Loser Besides The GOP Tuesday? Data Centers

While everyone talks about the implications for the Republican Party after Tuesday’s bruising defeat, there was another unsung loser on election night …

Voters nationwide made their disdain for the companies pushing America’s AI boom crystal clear.

Ten states considered 41 local ballot measures related to data centers Tuesday. Across all 50 measures tracked in 13 states this year, 46 of the 47 decided as of Wednesday sided with the common man against the tech giants.

Ohio alone proposed 11 charter amendments restricting data centers, and by all accounts, they’re all headed to victory, with some garnering over three-quarters of the vote.

The deep-pocketed industry didn’t go quietly.

Tech companies contributed more than $400,000 against the local restrictions that were on the ballot in Ohio.

In Oregon, opponents of data center restrictions raised $335,000 — in a town with less than 20,000 people.

The anti-data center proponents raised a measly $4,600 bucks, and still won.

Some quick math says the pro-tech side spent about $17 a person. Maybe $20 (enough for a burrito!) would have done the trick.

That ought to give you a little bit of hope in the American electorate.

The backlash shouldn’t surprise anyone.

At the Daily Caller, we’ve been sounding the alarm for months about the big concrete boxes full of wires being dropped across the country. American distaste for data centers has been clear long before Tuesday, despite Trump saying those of us who don’t support them are choosing “poverty, crime and squalor.”

Big Tech has spent years pitching AI as a miracle of technological advancement and economic prosperity. But Americans see through the facade. Who bears the burden of rising electricity bills, local water use, farmland loss, and god knows what other negative side effects? Well, the average man.

The industry also promised jobs, but except for some temporary construction jobs while the centers are being built, they don’t seem to have any long-term positive impact on employment. Once data centers are up and running, they typically only demand fewer than 100 employees for a facility the size of a small town.

An October ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll found 72 percent of Americans oppose building a new data center in their community, including 58 percent of Republicans, 76 percent of Independents and 81 percent of Democrats.

This isn’t a byproduct of the blue tsunami, but a resounding rebuke from the American people to the tech oligarchs forcing their clankers upon us.

Americans ranked AI and data centers in their top three issues leading up to the election, according to a USC Annenberg survey. Some 77 percent said the government was doing too little to regulate data centers; on election night, voters took the problem into their own hands.

There’s a larger point to be made here, one Washington would be wise to pay attention to.

They are exceptionally good at exploiting partisan divides: culture wars, personal disagreements between politicians, and lawfare, to name a few.

But they don’t pay as much attention to issues Americans largely agree on: corporate accountability, reining in special interest groups, money in politics, and affordability.

The American people’s clear rejection of data centers is an excellent example of what is possible when we find common ground and say no to corporate America.

Some Democrats saw that frustration and used it on the campaign trail. Whether they’ll turn that electoral boost into real policy remains to be seen, but it should be a lesson to politicos everywhere: our frustrations are clear; you just have to listen.

Meanwhile, a server farm doesn’t know a Republican from a Democrat, but it sure knows how to run up your electric bill. And when the everyday man bears the burden, we can find common ground, even when Washington’s political machine can’t.

EXCLUSIVE: Trump ‘Will Never Allow For Mass Amnesty’ After Floating Working With Dems On Immigration — Ashley Brasfield, Daily Caller

Following some late-night election calls into Fox News, conservatives were scratching their heads at the president’s intentions when he signaled he’d be willing to work with congressional Democrats on immigration. The vice president’s post-election diagnosis calling for stronger immigration enforcement added to the mixed signals. The Daily Caller’s Ashley Brasfield digs into the Trump White House’s approach to immigration once Democrats regain control of Congress in January.

Department Of War’s Absurd Answer To Blue Tsunami: A Podcast About How Much Brad Cooper Loves French Fries — John Loftus, Daily Caller

In the midst of a costly war hurting Americans at the pump, the Pentagon has unveiled its latest gift to the American people: a podcast. And not just any podcast: a sit-down with the top military brass running point on the Iran War. The subject matter? Adm. Brad Cooper’s love for French fries. Read more from the Daily Caller’s own John Loftus as he dives into the absurdity of it all.

Republicans Know They Got an ‘Ass Kicking,’ But Not What to Do About It — Igor Bobic, Al Weaver, The Washington Sun

The blame game has begun, and the justifications are … wide-ranging. Republicans across the country are offering up their best guess as to why the GOP endured one of the worst election nights in history; some say Trump’s obsession with his ballroom, others say gas prices, or maybe tariffs. Igor Bobic and Al Weaver at The Washington Sun break down the myriad explanations coming from Republicans on Capitol Hill.

College Republicans’ Populist Faction Makes Stunning Break With Trump Over Midterms, Broken Promises — John Loftus, Daily Caller

Tuesday night was a reckoning for Republicans and one of the largest groups of young conservatives is making their post-election diagnosis clear. The College Republican Patriot Coalition blamed the losses squarely on President Trump and the Republican Party. The letter included dozens of signatories from across the country. The Caller’s John Loftus breaks down their message to the president and what young conservative voters writ large are taking away from election night.

The 2026 Trump Collapse: Anatomy Of A Republican Disaster — Ryan Girdusky, Daily Wire

Most Republicans will have their names floated in the post-election blame game; consultant Ryan Girdusky makes sure President Trump is on that list in his latest Daily Wire op-ed. From the Iran War to tariffs and disastrous candidates, Girdusky argues that the commander-in-chief spent the last year and a half dismantling the very coalition that put him in the White House just two years ago.

news.originalContent:
Trump has three options to affect legislation, say analysts: veto legislation, enforce executive orders or make deals.

As the United States midterm election results landed late on Tuesday night, United States President Donald Trump took a phone call from the news outlet Politico.

A wave for the Democratic Party had sunk Trump’s Republican Party. For the first time in his two stints as president, Trump’s Republican Party no longer controlled either chamber of Congress.

But in the phone interview, Trump put on a brave face — and offered an olive branch: He said that he would be willing to work with Democrats.

“They’ve already called, and they want to work with me. I have the right to veto everything, but I don’t want to be just sitting there for two years just vetoing everything,” he said.

While a handful of seats remain to be counted, the Democrats have won comfortable majorities in both the House of Representatives, where they have secured at least 253 seats out of 435, and in the Senate, where they have won at least 54 out of 100.

Trump has since posted a picture on his Truth Social account using the Make America Great Again red baseball hat to read “VETO”. Despite the Democrats’ success, as president, Trump holds broad executive authority, with Article 1, Section 7 of the US Constitution stipulating that the president has the power to reject legislation passed by Congress through a veto.

Congress can override the veto, but would need to have a two-thirds majority, something that the Democrats do not have in either chamber.

But Trump’s comments to Politico underscore an alternate possibility — the president may pick and choose when to veto, and when to work with Democrats.

As it stands, Trump has three options: veto legislation, enforce executive orders or make deals.

Since Trump was inaugurated in January 2025, he has passed 292 executive orders: 67 this year and 225 last year, according to the Federal Register.

But now, according to Andrew Proctor, a lecturer in US politics at University College London, Trump has even less leverage than before with Congress.

“I think the biggest thing is we’re probably going to see a decent amount of gridlock. The Democrats are going to try to pass policies, but he’s got the power to veto them, and Democrats don’t have enough seats in either chamber to overcome any vetoes that he has,” Proctor said.

“So that raises questions about, will he try to work with the Democrats at all on passing legislation? I think recent history says that’s unlikely.”

Still, some Democrats have said that they would work with the president to advance programmes central to their campaign promises.

Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed, the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, has already said he could work with Trump  — even though the US president had used racist and Islamophobic rhetoric to target El-Sayed during the campaign.

El-Sayed told MSNOW on Thursday that if Trump was interested in “getting money out of politics, putting money in pockets and passing Medicare for All, that’s what I ran to do, and I’m looking forward to working with anyone who is willing to do that”.

“He is the president of the United States,” he said. “I’m going to be one United States senator, and if he’s interested in working on issues that I want to work on – getting more people healthcare, ending the Medicare cuts, ending the stupid war, stopping these stupid tariffs with Canada – then let’s talk about doing that and go and deliver for the public.”

Progressive Senator Bernie Sanders has also said, in recent interviews, that he would not rule out Trump signing onto a Medicare for All bill if Democrats pass it in both chambers of Congress. He described Trump as a “politician” who was not “too ideological”.

Proctor argued that Trump could indeed make a deal with the Democrats based on how good it could make him look, but that getting Medicare for All passed in the next two years appeared unlikely.

“I do think that a place where common ground could emerge on healthcare is rolling back, specifically the sort of subsidies that were cut” under Trump’s earlier legislation, he said. “So that would make healthcare more affordable for millions of Americans.”

Proctor pointed out that some Republicans in 2025 had said they were willing to negotiate with Democrats on healthcare reforms.

“That didn’t end up happening, but I could imagine that might be a place for healthcare-specific policy where we could see something emerge,” he said. “I don’t think that a broader healthcare debate on passing Medicare for All, though, is really in the cards.”

Though Trump has said he would be willing to use veto, he has historically not been among the most avid proponents of the practice.

He has so far used the veto twice in this term, and used it 10 times during his first term. Joe Biden used it 12 times in his single term, while Barack Obama used the veto a dozen times over two terms.

Overall, the presidential use of the veto has declined with time: Bill Clinton vetoed legislation 37 times between 1993 and 2001. His predecessor, George HW Bush, used it 44 times in his single term — almost once a month. Ronald Reagan used it 78 times over his two terms.

But Proctor said that Republicans also have a different tool to try and block legislation. That is the filibuster, a tactic that delays a vote on a specific piece of legislation by using an extended debate, which would impact the Democrats’ ability to get something passed.

“This is what they did to [former President Barack] Obama,” Proctor told Al Jazeera. “Senate Republicans will probably try to do the same thing, and it also means that we don’t even get to the point of Trump having the power to veto because the legislation never reaches him in the first place.”

Since the Democrats swept the midterms on Tuesday, calls for investigations against the administration have already emerged.

In his first term, Trump was impeached twice — first for the abuse of power and obstruction of Congress, and the second time for “inciting” the US Capitol riots.

On Tuesday night, US Representative Robert Garcia, who is set to become chairman of the House Oversight Committee, wrote on X: “LAWYER UP.” Senator Ron Wyden, who is expected to lead the Senate Finance Committee, wrote in a post on X: “Subpoenas.”

However, the Trump administration has already denied any wrongdoing.

“If Democrats choose to pursue sham investigations and radical left policies, they are choosing to work against the American people,” said White House spokesperson Lauren Bis on Wednesday.

Reports also suggest that impeachment proceedings against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth might be imminent, over the Iran war that Trump and other Republicans have blamed for the party’s losses.
